title: DAY 3 — LESSON 4: ASKING QUESTIONS INSTEAD OF MAKING ASSUMPTIONS

options: A fact that has been carefully verified
A conclusion accepted without enough information to confirm it
A clear instruction from a supervisor

questions.prompt: A colleague does not greet you. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Avoid immediately concluding that the colleague dislikes you
Tell other staff that the colleague is disrespectful
Refuse to cooperate with the colleague

questions.prompt: A client asks to change a booking. What should the receptionist do?
options: Assume the client wants another therapist
Ask exactly what the client wants to change and confirm the details

questions.prompt: Which question is most constructive when a task is incomplete?
options: Why are you always so lazy?
Was there a difficulty that prevented the task from being completed?
Don't you know how to do your job?

questions.prompt: What does the CHECK method encourage?
options: Considering facts, holding back assumptions, enquiring, confirming and responding constructively
Accepting the first explanation that comes to mind
Avoiding questions because they show uncertainty
